articles.title: I travel 200,000 miles a year. These are the five carry-on suitcases I actually trust
articles.summary: In an endless sea of suitcase options, these are the best to save you time and money, including a top pick made of recycled plastic. The best travel backpack. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: There are few worse feelings than climbing off an all-day flight, shambling on down to baggage claim, and then watching each and every one of your fellow passengers gleefully grab their bag and disappear, while yours is nowhere to be found. The devastating realization that your checked suitcase didn’t make it is a strong enough blow to turn the sweetest of vacations sour.

I’ve been there, and that’s just one of the many reasons I never check a bag unless I absolutely have to. But living the carry-on life requires having the right suitcase, and there are hundreds and hundreds of choices out there. We tested 15 models and considered dozens more to find the perfect one for you.

I make my living as a freelance journalist, but finding the story often means hopping on a plane and jetting somewhere far away. I fly about 200,000 miles every year, endure 150 days away from home, and set down in a dozen countries or more.

articles.title: Game, set and tache: Carlos Alcaraz joins growing trend for a stylish top lip
articles.summary: Tennis superstar is latest celebrity to sport a ‘refined’ moustache which owes little to bushy Tom Selleck look. The tennis superstar Carlos Alcaraz might have been knocked out of the Shanghai Masters in straight sets earlier this week, but he did so sporting a moustache that became almost as…
body: “I always wanted to step on the court at least once with the moustache,” Alcaraz said. The Spaniard and his team had all agreed to take the facial-hair plunge if he won the Japan Open, which he did for a second straight year. “¡Bigotes para todos!” or “moustaches for everyone”, they apparently cheered at the end of the match.
At Milan fashion week last month, the Wuthering Heights star Jacob Elordi sported a thin strip of hair on his top lip as he watched his girlfriend, Kendall Jenner, model for the Bottega Veneta show.

A moustachioed Harry Styles is roughly halfway through his record-breaking 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden in New York. The actor Timothée Chalamet, who kept his Marty Supreme ’tache on throughout awards season, has been playing around with his facial hair again, adding a goatee.
On TikTok, gen Z men with moustaches are plentiful, as are tutorials for how to grow and style them – alongside almost as many videos from older generations questioning them.

articles.title: Judith Lucy on her cancer diagnosis: ‘I’m a bit over getting so much material out of my life’
articles.summary: One of Australia’s hardest-working comedians is still laughing at the timing of a breast cancer diagnosis just as she set out to launch a book about wellness. Two days out from surgery, she talks burnout, Buddhism and saying goodbye to her boobs. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: Judith Lucy cannot get a cold. A few hours before I’m due to meet her for a walk around the rose gardens and classic conservatory of the St Kilda Botanical Gardens, a stone’s throw from her home in Melbourne’s south-east, the beloved comedian is on a telehealth call from the front seat of her publicist’s car.

Her doctor needs to go over the results from the previous day’s scans to confirm everything is looking good – good enough to perform the double mastectomy they have planned for Friday, three weeks after she was diagnosed with breast cancer. The cancer isn’t appearing anywhere else on the scans, she learns, but a compromised immune system going into surgery would throw the whole thing out of whack. So with the blustery wind and grey skies at our backs, we retreat into her home instead. The walk up and down the hallway, from the front door of her lovely weatherboard cottage to the neat living room at the back will have to make do for our very short walk.
points: One of Australia’s hardest-working comedians is still laughing at the timing of a breast cancer diagnosis just as she set out to launch a book about wellness.

articles.title: How to dress a tech oligarch: The Social Reckoning’s costume designer on Zuckerberg’s style evolution
articles.summary: Susan Lyall worked with actor Jeremy Strong to research the Meta CEO’s favorite Nikes and luxury sweaters. The first Aaron Sorkin Facebook movie, 2010’s The Social Network, helped cement the early aughts image of Mark Zuckerberg rebelling against corporate norms in rumpled hoodies and T-shirts.
body: The follow-up, The Social Reckoning, is carbon-dated from 2019 to 2021. This is “post-hoodie”, as the movie’s costume designer, Susan Lyall, describes it, “post-thumbing his nose” to formality. It is also peak robot. Zuckerberg’s reserved wardrobe of suits or interchangeable long-sleeved shirts echo his chilling composure throughout, even as fury simmers under the surface.

The costume was based on deep research by Lyall and also by actor Jeremy Strong who, she says, is “very into costume”. Having worked together before, on the Sorkin movies Molly’s Game and The Trial of the Chicago 7, they would text a lot during the preparation process.

“He reaches out before I even get to reach out to him. It’s my third movie with him, so I’m pretty used to it. He’s very proactive. He’s one of my favourite actors because of that. He would know exactly where [Zuckerberg] wore what. He wanted the exact Nike shoe – the footwear was very important to him – and the exact Brunello Cucinelli T-shirt and sweater, and so on,” she says.

articles.title: 5 Lady Jacket Outfits to Wear This Fall, According to the Street Style Set
articles.summary: From everyday denim to tailored trousers, discover five fresh ways to style fall’s must-have lady jacket—all inspired by the street style set.
body: Prim and proper? Not quite! This fall the classic lady jacket is getting a modern makeover, with purposefully shrunken silhouettes emerging as one of the season’s biggest outerwear trends. Naturally, the street style set quickly embraced the look, styling the traditionally feminine staple in fresh ways throughout fashion month.

We saw it more than once with denim. For example, Vogue ’s executive fashion director, Lisa Aiken, gave Kallmeyer’s gilded jacquard jacket a daytime spin with wide-leg blue jeans and black pumps. British Vogue ’s Chioma Nnadi, meanwhile, gave a pink lady jacket a maximalist feel by pairing it with a denim midiskirt and lace-up flats. Elsewhere on the streets of Paris, one off-duty model sported a classic black take with straight-leg blue jeans and, for an unexpected touch of luxury, elbow-length leather gloves.
But with jeans isn’t the only way to wear them. Below are five outfit ideas to make it your own, whether you’re heading into the office (hello, new power suits!) or out for drinks downtown.
points: From everyday denim to tailored trousers, discover five fresh ways to style fall’s must-have lady jacket—all inspired by the street style set.

articles.title: The Model Off-Duty Uniform, Decoded
articles.summary: For your next weekend look, take a cue from the model off-duty playbook. Their personal brand of nonchalant cool is easily recreated with these simple basics.
body: Just like designers, stylists, and armies of interns, fashion week simply wouldn’t exist without models. On the runway, a model embodies a designer’s vision. Outside the shows, however, the vision is all their own. Models in their “ off-duty ” element have long been a fixation among the fashion crowd, infusing the street style scene with their own brand of nonchalant cool.

The model-off-duty aesthetic is hard to define—part of it, certainly, is the attitude—but there are certain patterns we see again and again. Easy basics are key. Models love tees and knits that strike a balance between comfortable and cool. Relaxed pants are essential, too—tough denim, cargos, and pleated trousers are reliable go-tos. On the footwear front, models tend to favor options that can easily take them from show to show, like sneakers, loafers, and boots.

As straightforward as the building blocks may seem, the looks are rarely boring, and that’s what makes them so fun to recreate. Mixed in among the casual separates, you’ll often find an It bag, a great leather jacket, or another standout piece that gives the whole thing personality. The looks below prove it—see and shop them for yourself.
points: For your next weekend look, take a cue from the model off-duty playbook.

articles.title: Now Might Be a Good Time for a Talisman
articles.summary: From ancient Egypt to the modern age, amulets and talismans have played a leading role in the spiritual landscape. Here’s why protective objects are capturing our imaginations today.
body: In November 1922, archaeologist Howard Carter descended a limestone passage in Egypt’s Valley of the Kings. Holding a flame up in the darkness, he peered through a small hole chiseled into a sealed door. When asked if he could see anything, Carter famously replied, “Yes, wonderful things.”

More than one hundred objects were discovered within the linen bandages of King Tutankhamun ’s mummy, including an abundance of amulets that Carter declared were “intended to protect against injury on that journey in the underworld.” Scarabs, serpents, vultures, lunar ornaments, ancient gods like Horus and Anubis carved from gold and lapis lazuli —all strategically placed on various points along the body.
Over 3,300 years later, these kinds of symbolic objects aren’t relics from a bygone era—rather, they play an ongoing role in our spiritual landscape.

articles.title: A Classic Newport, Rhode Island Wedding With Tennis-Inspired Details and a Performance by Norah Jones
articles.summary: Hannah Mullin and Sean O'Connell's Newport wedding weekend featured intricate, custom décor and a first dance to “Come Away With Me” performed by Norah Jones.
body: The celebration would span two days of events, beginning with a rehearsal dinner and welcome party at the Tennis Hall of Fame complete with an entire custom merch suite and tennis-inspired details. “Me and Sarah always laugh with one another when we look back and realize this all came into place from only three to four inspiration pictures from me,” the bride says. Design was an important factor in planning the weekend, with blooming florals from Stoneblossom, custom illustrations by Champagne and Ink, and transformative décor crafted by Ryan Designs.

“What makes this experience so unforgettable isn’t just the extraordinary talent of every person involved, but their kindness,” reflects Hannah. “Every vendor became more than someone we hired. They became collaborators, cheerleaders, and friends.” She adds, “Finally, none of this would have lived on the way it has without Stephanie Vegliante. Long after the flowers have faded and the music has ended, it is her photographs that allow us to return to these moments again and again.”

articles.title: 20 Extraordinary Shops Worth Traveling For, Chosen by The Shopkeepers
articles.summary: From 100-year-old family-run operations to contemporary boutiques, these beautiful shops each offer a distinct sense of place and a dedication to craft.
body: When distinguishing a great shop from a good one, several qualities come to mind. Perhaps the storefront is as beautiful as it is historic, with perfectly-aged signage alluding to a storied past. Once inside, you may find a hawk-eyed curation of many goods or a passionate pursuit of a single good. And the shopkeeper, the glue to hold it all together, can bring an irreplaceable sense of place and reason to stay just a moment more—or both.

While shops can close or evolve, Flynn is confident their legacies will remain. "[The book] is a tribute, and I think they’re shops people can always look to to be inspired.” From a 237-year-old candle shop in Lisbon to a townhouse-turned-textiles-museum in Istanbul, explore 20 of the most beautiful shops in the world below, courtesy of Flynn.

articles.title: The Adventure-Ready Samsung Galaxy Watch Is Over $175 Off Right Now
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication. Samsung announced the Galaxy Watch Ultra in the summer of 2024, and then refreshed it in August of 2025 with double the storage and new color options.
body: The Galaxy Watch Ultra excels over other watches in one key aspect: its outdoorsy features. If you're an avid hiker or an athlete who spends long hours outdoors, this is a worthwhile choice. Like any good rugged watch, this one is tough, made out of Grade 4 titanium, and has an IP68 water- and dust-resistant rating. You can also take it up high altitudes (up to 9,000 meters) and it can withstand up to 10ATM of pressure (about 330 feet underwater). You also get a built-in siren in case of emergencies. The screen is a 1.47-inch Super AMOLED display, brighter than previous Samsung AMOLED smartwatches. The only downside is that it comes in just one size—47mm.

The watch runs WearOS from Samsung and comes with 2GB of RAM and 64GB of storage. The 590mAh battery is one of the best for its price point, making it perfect for prolonged outdoor use. If you don't use any power-saving modes, it'll last 60 hours, but it can go up to 100 hours if you're conservative.

articles.summary: It’s way too easy for my kitchen to become cluttered. Cut to me swimming through pots, pans, and kitchen tools in my cabinets as I try to find the exact thing I’m looking for (that I swear is in there!).
body: One area that could use a little organizational help right now? The under-sink cabinet. It’s currently a mess of plastic grocery bags we plan to reuse, dish sponges, cleaning supplies, zip-top bags, and more. That’s where this Delamu Under-Sink Organizer set would make a huge difference. And bonus: It’s under $50.

Delamu offers lots of organizational items for the home, including cord hiders, makeup organizers, and, of course, under-sink organizers. The particular under-sink organizer I’m eyeing is one Amazon shoppers have bought more than 3,000 of in the past month alone, and I can totally see why.

The cream-colored organizer comes with light wood handles that look beautiful. It also has two tiers (with drawers!) that make it easy to reach cleaning supplies tucked way in the back. Plus, you get two organizers in this $40 set, so your under-sink cabinet will be neat and orderly on both sides.

Another cool feature? It has five different height options — from 13.8- to 17.8 inches — to basically custom-fit any cabinet. If you’re looking to get your cabinets organized before the chaos of the holidays sets in, then you’ll want to grab this under-sink organizer set, stat!
